extractedItems.title: What is a club-length?
extractedItems.question: When measuring a relief area, what does 'club-length' mean?

choices.text: The player's longest club, except the putter
Any club from the bag
Only the driver
Only the putter

extractedItems.explanation: A club-length is defined as the player's longest club except the putter.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A golf bag with clubs and one club laid out on the grass to show its full length.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Golf bag with a club on the ground to show club-length.

extractedItems.title: Correct way to drop a ball
extractedItems.question: How must you drop a ball when taking relief, according to the Rules?

choices.text: From knee height
From shoulder height
By placing it on the ground
By tossing it gently

extractedItems.explanation: The ball must be dropped from knee height in the relief area.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer dropping a golf ball from knee height onto the fairway.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Golfer dropping a ball from knee height.

extractedItems.title: When must a ball be dropped again?
extractedItems.question: If a dropped ball hits the player before it hits the ground, what should you do?

choices.text: Drop the ball again
Play the ball as it lies
Add a penalty and play on
Ask a referee

extractedItems.explanation: If the ball touches the player before hitting the ground, it must be dropped again.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl drops a ball, but it bounces off her shoe before hitting the ground.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Golf ball hitting the player's foot before touching the ground.

extractedItems.title: What happens if the dropped ball rolls out of the relief area?
extractedItems.question: After you drop the ball in the relief area, it rolls out. What should you do?

choices.text: Drop the ball again
Place the ball where it stopped
Play it from where it rolled to
Move it back and play from original spot

extractedItems.explanation: If the ball rolls out of the relief area after a drop, you must drop it again.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen boy drops a ball and it rolls away, out of a marked relief area.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Golf ball rolling out of the marked area after being dropped.

extractedItems.title: What do you do if the ball won't stay in the relief area?
extractedItems.question: If you drop the ball twice and it still won’t stay in the relief area, what do you do next?

choices.text: Place the ball at the spot where it first touched the ground after the second drop
Drop it again
Place it on the nearest fairway
Take a penalty and continue

extractedItems.explanation: If the ball does not stay in the relief area after two drops, you place it where it first touched the ground after the second drop.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen girl places a golf ball carefully on the grass in the relief area after dropping twice.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Golfer placing ball on the spot after failed drops.

Any club you choose from your bag
The length of your driver only
The length of your putter

reviewedItems.title: Correct way to drop a ball
reviewedItems.question: According to the Rules of Golf, how should you drop a ball when taking relief?

choices.text: Let it fall from knee height
Let it fall from shoulder height
Place it gently on the ground by hand
Toss it upwards from knee height

reviewedItems.explanation: You need to drop the ball straight down from knee height so it falls through the air without touching you or your equipment.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage golfer standing on the fairway drops a golf ball from knee height.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Golfer dropping a golf ball from knee height.

reviewedItems.title: When must a ball be dropped again?
reviewedItems.question: If you drop the ball but it touches you or your equipment before hitting the ground, what must you do?

choices.text: Drop the ball again
Play the ball as it lies
Add a penalty and play on
Ask a referee and wait

reviewedItems.explanation: If the dropped ball touches you or your equipment before hitting the ground, you must drop it again without penalty.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl drops a ball, but the ball bounces off her shoe before touching the ground on the fairway.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Golf ball making contact with the golfer's foot before it lands.

reviewedItems.title: What happens if the dropped ball rolls out of the relief area?
reviewedItems.question: After you drop your ball in the correct place, it rolls out of the relief area. What do you do next?

choices.text: Drop the ball again in the relief area
Place the ball where it stopped
Hit it from where it finished
Move it back to the original spot

reviewedItems.explanation: If your dropped ball comes to rest outside the relief area, you must drop it again within the relief area.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage golfer watches as a dropped ball rolls out of a clearly marked relief area on the fairway.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Golf ball rolling out of a marked relief area after a drop.

reviewedItems.title: What do you do if the ball won't stay in the relief area?
reviewedItems.question: If you drop the ball twice and it still won’t stay in the relief area, what does the Rule require you to do?

choices.text: Place the ball on the spot where it first touched the ground after the second drop
Drop it a third time
Place it anywhere in the relief area
Take a penalty and continue

reviewedItems.explanation: If a dropped ball twice fails to stay within the defined relief area, you must place it on the spot where it touched the ground after the second drop.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage golfer places a golf ball carefully on the fairway at the spot it last landed after two drops.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Golfer placing a ball at the spot after failed drops in the relief area.
